Case :- Application U/S 528 Bnss No. - 21572 of 2025

Applicant :- Ashok Jain
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Kuldeep Kumar,Rahul Jain
Counsel for Opposite Party :- Pandey Balkrishna,G.A.

Hon'ble Vikram D. Chauhan,J.
1.

Heard learned counsel for the Applicant, Sri Amarendra Nath Singh, learned Senior Advocate
assisted by Sri Pandey Balkrishna, learned counsel for opposite party no. 2 and learned Aga for the
State.

2.  This application has been filed by the applicant for quashing the impugned order dated 03.03.2025 as well as memorandum order dated 03.03.2025 passed by Additional Session/Fast Track Court First, Court No. 1, Prayagraj in Session Trial No. 1393 of 2024 (State Vs. Vaibhav Jain and others) arising out of Case Crime No. 08 of 2022, under Sections 498-A, 376, 354 IPC and Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station-Kotwali, District - Prayagraj and to quash the entire further proceeding of Session Trial No. 1393 of 2024 (State Vs. Vaibhav Jain and others)
arising out of Case Crime No. 08 of 2022, under Sections 498-A, 376, 354 IPC and Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station - Kotwali, District - Prayagraj.

3. Learned counsel for applicant submits that initially first information report was lodged on 15.1.2022 under Sections 498A, 376, 377, 323, 354 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 D.P. sentences.text: Learned counsel for applicant further submits that present criminal proceedings have been drawn as a result of Section 12 of Hindu Marriage Act being filed by husband on 21.12.2021 and the present first information report has been lodged on 15.1.2022.

Learned counsel for applicant further submits that solely on account of the fact that husband has preferred application under Section 12 of Hindu Marriage Act, present criminal proceedings has been lodged and as such, the same are abuse of process of law.

Learned counsel for applicant further submits that on perusal of first information report would go to show that there is no time and date fixed with regard to offence although against applicant allegation is with regard to demand of dowry and sexual assault are alleged, however, charge sheet in the present case has been submitted against applicant only in respect of Section 498A I.P.C. and 3/4 D.P. Act.

Learned counsel for applicant further submits that statement of victim has been recorded under Sections 161 Cr.P.C.
as well as under Section 164 Cr.P.C.
3-A.
Learned counsel for the applicant further submits that none of the witnesses have supported the case of informant with regard to allegation under Section 376 I.P.C. except victim herself.

Learned counsel for applicant on the strength of judgment of the Apex Court in Suman Mishra and Ors. Vs. The State of Uttar Pradesh & Anr., 2025 0 Supreme(SC) 328 submits that allegations are general and omnibus against applicant and the present proceedings are vexatious proceedings.

entities.text: Suman Mishra and Ors. Vs. The State of Uttar Pradesh & Anr., 2025 0 Supreme(SC) 328
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for applicant further submits that applicant is aged about 68 years.

Learned counsel for applicant submits that against the order rejecting discharge application, applicant had filed Criminal Revision No.6354 of 2024 (Ashok Jain Vs. State of U.P. and another), however, the aforesaid criminal revision was dismissed as infructuous by order dated 1.7.2025.

entities.text: Criminal Revision No.6354 of 2024 (Ashok Jain Vs. State of U.P. and another)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for applicant further submits that present application under Section 528 BNSS arises out of impugned order dated 3.3.2025 by which the court concerned has directed framing of charge against applicant under Sections 376, 498A I.P.C. and Section 3/4 D.P. Act.

Learned counsel for applicant while challenging the aforesaid order submits that once there was no date and time of incident in the first information report then the charge under Section 376 I.P.C. could not have been framed, more particularly, when the Investigating Officer after investigation had not filed charge sheet under Section 376 I.P.C. against applicant and the charge sheet was only filed under Section 498A I.P.C. and Section 3/4 D.P. Act.

3-B. Learned counsel for applicant has relied upon the judgment of this Court in Smt. Usha Vs. State of U.P. and another, 2024 0 Supreme(All) 735 to submit that no opportunity of hearing was granted while passing the impugned order dated 3.3.2025.

entities.text: Smt. Usha Vs. State of U.P. and another, 2024 0 Supreme(All) 735
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for applicant was asked to show prejudice caused by not providing opportunity of hearing as the discharge application of applicant was rejected and aforesaid order stood finalized by dismissal of Criminal Revision No. 6354 of 2024,
learned counsel for applicant only submits that under Section 528 BNSS, applicant can challenge the entire proceedings at any point of time by referring to Suman Mishra (supra) case.

Learned counsel for applicant further submits that victim had never consented for medical examination and as such, aforesaid circumstance would be read against the victim, which would be an indicative factor that present prosecution is vexatious in nature.

4. Sri Amarendra Nath Singh, learned Senior Advocate assisted by Sri Pandey Balkrishna, learned counsel for opposite party no. 2 has opposed the present application and submits that discharge Ashok Jain vs State Of U.P. And Another on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18142160/
2 application of husband has been rejected by order dated 19.12.2024 in Application under Section 482 No. 35886 of 2024 (Vaibhav Jain Vs. State of U.P.) and the same has attained finality.

sentences.text: It is further submitted that insofar as criminal revision filed by applicant against the order rejecting discharge application, the same has already been rendered infructuous, however, applicant was granted opportunity to file recall application in the aforesaid revision, if any, issue remains undecided.
He further submits that no recall application has been preferred on behalf of applicant.
Learned Senior Advocate further submits that statement of victim has been recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. where specific allegations have been made against applicant with regard to rape.

Learned Senior Advocate further submits that it is a settled law that the statement of victim itself is sufficient for prosecution in respect of allegation of rape and as such, the court concerned has committed no error in framing the charge under Section 376 I.P.C. against applicant.

4-A. Learned Senior Advocate for opposite party no. 2 further submits that if opportunity of hearing was not granted to the accused then it is for the accused to state what prejudice has been caused and learned counsel for applicant has not shown any prejudice in respect of the order once there is a clear evidence prior to submission of charge sheet by way of statement of victim under Section 164 Cr.P.C.
It is also submitted that the court is not bound by the charge sheet submitted and it is always open for the court to frame charge in accordance with law.
5. Learned A.G.A. has opposed the submission and has submitted that the impugned order has been passed in accordance with law.

6. It is to be seen that present first information report has been lodged on 15.1.2022 under Sections 498A, 376, 377, 323, 354 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 D.P. Act against Vishal Jain, husband, Vaibhav Jain,
brother-in-law, Kiran Jain, mother-in-law and Ashok Jain (applicant), who is father-in-law.

It is further to be seen that perusal of first information report insofar as applicant is concerned, the allegations were that applicant was misbehaving and threatening the victim and demanding dowry.
There was no allegation of rape in the first information report against applicant.
However, when the statement of victim was recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., she has specifically stated that allegation of rape as of 3.11.2020 at 11.00 p.m.
Although, learned counsel for applicant has pressed that allegations in the first information report are general and vague in nature.
However, statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. shows specific allegation with regard to rape.

The statement of victim under Section 164 Cr.P.C. may be an essential circumstance at the stage of trial, however, at the stage of framing of charge, trial court has to see the material available on record.
Statement of victim under Section 164 Cr.P.C. is an essential material in respect of allegation.

7. It is further to be seen that in respect of question of opportunity of hearing prior to passing of impugned order, it is true that the accused has a right to be heard prior to passing of impugned order, however, once the accused put to challenge the aforesaid order, it is required to show by the accused as to what prejudice has been caused, by demonstrating from the record that there is no evidence.

Certainly when the evidence and statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. is available and such statement has not been denied by the applicant although learned counsel for applicant has stated that in the first information report general and omnibus allegation has been made and except the victim no other witnesses has supported the prosecution case with regard to rape against applicant.

3 8.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is settled law

that the statement of victim itself is sufficient for prosecution of an accused in respect of rape charge although in the trial, the aforesaid statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. is required to be tested by cross examination.

At this stage, it cannot be said that the trial court has committed any error in law in framing the charge under Section 376 I.P.C.
9.
It is further to be seen that if the victim has denied medical examination then the aforesaid itself may be a circumstance at the stage of trial.

However, at this stage, it cannot be held that mere denial of medical examination more particularly when the allegation of rape is of 3.11.2020 whereas the first information report is of 15.1.2022 any material prejudice could have been shown to be caused,
as after such a long period, it may not be possible to give any report on the question of rape.

10. It is further to be seen that the applicant against the order rejecting discharge application applicant had preferred a Criminal Revision No. 6354 of 2024, which was rendered infructuous as the charge has been framed.
However, the Court by in it's order dated 1.7.2025 has specifically permitted the applicant to file recall application if any issue remains pending.
The applicant has not availed the opportunity given in the criminal revision.
The rejection of the discharge application has attained finality.
Neither the recall application was filed bringing to notice of the revisional court.
The aforesaid issue at the stage of framing of charge, the evidence which is available on record is to be seen and the charge framed under Section 376 I.P.C. requires no interference.

Insofar as argument of learned counsel for applicant that the trial is vexatious in nature as application under Section 12 of Hindu Marriage Act has been filed by the accused at prior point of time that may be an important material at the stage of trial.

However, this Court cannot hold a mini trial at this stage and more particularly when the order rejecting discharge application of the applicant as well as of the husband confirmed by this Court and no opportunity of recall application has been availed by the applicant.
11.
It is to be seen that in the present case no prayer challenging the summoning order has been made although the entire criminal proceedings have been sought to be quashed.
Once there is no challenge to summoning order then criminal proceedings cannot be quashed without challenging the summoning order/cognizance order.
Further discharge application which was rejected by the court concerned stood finalised and as such at this stage the entire criminal proceedings cannot be quashed.

12. It is further to be seen that on perusal of the impugned order as well as the charge framed would go to show that counsel for the accused were given opportunity of hearing prior to passing of the impugned order.

If the applicant were to challenge the findings in the impugned order with regard to opportunity of hearing then the remedy would be to file an application before the court concerned which in the present case has not been made nor any ground has been shown as to why the impugned order is bad in law.
13. Accordingly, the present application under Section 528 BNSS sans merit and is dismissed.
However, liberty is granted to applicant to raise all the aforesaid issues at the stage of trial.
